brief.headline: Memory pricing acceleration continues; HBM supply locked, CoWoS easing 2H; hyperscaler capex $725B in 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="12-6,12-7">DDR4 8Gb rose 14.3% MoM to $24 in July, while NAND 128Gb MLC hit $30.1</cite>, marking 19 consecutive months of gains. <cite index="15-1,15-2">TrendForce projects Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15% QoQ</cite>, with <cite index="8-3,8-13">top three memory makers pre-sold on full HBM output for 2026, Micron guiding 68% Q2 gross margin</cite>. <cite index="27-2,27-3">Hyperscalers spending ~$725B in 2026 (Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, Microsoft $120B)</cite>, up 77% YoY. <cite index="29-11">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to ~10% by end-2026</cite> as <cite index="36-1">monthly capacity scales to 120-130K wafers</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix commanded 57% HBM revenue share in Q4 2025 vs Samsung 22%</cite>, and <cite index="5-3">channel checks indicate Hynix will hold ~50% HBM market share in 2026</cite>. <cite index="8-9">SK Hynix is the only supplier delivering both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale</cite>, while <cite index="5-4">Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification with Nvidia, facing pricing pushback</cite>. Relative: long Hynix / short Samsung on HBM share delta and qualification timing gap. Hynix better positioned for Nvidia Rubin and MI400 ramps; Samsung risk if HBM4 certification slips or pricing concessions required to win share.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="8-5">Global memory market under acute strain as HBM prioritization tightens mainstream DRAM/NAND for consumer and industrial electronics</cite>. <cite index="11-9,11-10">AI inference and hyperscale demand keeps DRAM/NAND supply constrained; capacity shift to higher-margin server products leaves less for consumer, preventing price declines despite PC/smartphone demand softening</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historical norms</cite>. <cite index="6-6,6-7">Industry belief: AI upended boom-bust cyclicality; structural supply shortage could keep prices elevated for years</cite>, though <cite index="6-11">scope for production to increase meaningfully over next 3 years, especially if AI demand grows at more normal pace</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-3">HBM3E remains dominant AI memory through year with pricing power intact until new capacity post-2027; top three already allocated full HBM output</cite>. <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects minimal to modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs 2025</cite> as <cite index="5-4">Nvidia negotiates with Hynix, Samsung, Micron on HBM3E pricing</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Micron integrated HBM3E 36GB 12-high into AMD MI350 Series</cite>; <cite index="1-6,1-7">AMD MI400 features 12 HBM4 stacks (432GB, 19.6 TB/s bandwidth), each delivering ~1.6 TB/s</cite>. <cite index="4-5">Micron HBM4 designed for Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs, reaching >2.8 TB/s bandwidth</cite>. Supply bottleneck easing but remains tight.

news_pulse.headline: July DRAM, NAND prices hit record highs; DDR4 8Gb +14.3% MoM to $24
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum intact into Q3; AI/server demand overwhelming consumer softness. Samsung/Hynix revenue and margin upside if ASP trajectory holds through Q3.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Price increases decelerating from Q1/Q2 peaks (90-95% QoQ in Q1, 58-75% in Q2) but still robust. Margin expansion continues but at slower pace; watch for demand elasticity.

news_pulse.headline: Top 3 memory makers pre-sold full 2026 HBM output; Micron guiding 68% Q2 GM
news_pulse.implication: HBM = zero-sum vs mainstream DRAM/NAND. Every HBM wafer crowds out PC/smartphone memory. Validates gross margin expansion story; Hynix/Samsung HBM mix shift = structural re-rating.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex ~$725B in 2026 (Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, MSFT $120B), +77% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented infrastructure build validates multi-year memory demand visibility. Counterpoint: $600B revenue gap (Sequoia) and 46% capex-revenue divergence (Allianz) vs 2001 telecom (32%) raises macro risk if monetization stalls.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix holds ~50% 2026 HBM market share; only supplier delivering HBM3E + HBM4 at scale
news_pulse.implication: Hynix HBM leadership defensible through 2026-27. Samsung playing catch-up on HBM3E qualification; Samsung HBM4 certification timeline vs Hynix = key swing factor for relative returns.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026; capacity 120-140K wpm
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing 2H26; Nvidia/AMD GPU shipment constraints loosen. Positive for HBM attach rate and Samsung/Hynix HBM volume ramp, but could shift pricing leverage back to hyperscalers if GPU supply exceeds near-term demand.

news_pulse.headline: Memory shortages expected through 2027; pricing power stronger than historical industry norms
news_pulse.implication: Structural shift thesis: AI breaks boom-bust cycle. Bullish for sustained margins, but risks production expansion (2027+) or demand normalization. Monitor PC/smartphone sell-through and hyperscaler ROI scrutiny.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix YTD stock returns +114%, +186%; Micron/SanDisk +141%, +156%
news_pulse.implication: Extreme YTD gains embed high expectations. Investors pricing structural upcycle, but valuation risk if AI capex slows or TurboQuant-style efficiency breakthroughs reduce memory intensity. Deutsche Bank flags continuous AI-related disruption risk.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KOSPI 200 futures or options data in payload. Macro: monitor won stability (USD/KRW) and KOSPI beta. Structural long volatility in memory names given binary HBM qualification outcomes (Samsung HBM3E/HBM4 certification with Nvidia) and hyperscaler capex sustainability risk. Pair trade: long Hynix / short Samsung via ADRs (HXSCL / SSNLF) or Korea-listed if liquidity permits; hedge macro via KOSPI 200 futures if capex fatigue narrative accelerates.
